Persistent failures on both counts and attributes require a stronger composition strategy with pairwise layout, exact-count emphasis, and negative clauses against extras or merged instances.

Emphasizing spotted flamingos could accidentally spread patterning to other objects unless attribute binding stays object-specific.
Making turtles visibly glass could reduce turtle recognizability unless they remain clear turtle shapes.
